svg.title: Allocate $200,000 Before Making the First Offer
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-two-hundred-thousand-dollar-startup-stack; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate $200,000 Before Making the First Offer; subtitle: Four nonoverlapping capital buckets within the $50,000–$400,000 range; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: This single startup allocation totals $200,000 and sits inside the canonical $50,000–$400,000 capital range. Values are USD capital allocations, not annual expenses or recognized revenue. Acquisition capital remains inventory until disposition; unused reserves remain cash. Recycling sale proceeds is required to support annual purchases above the initial inventory bucket.; caption: $140,000 + $20,000 + $15,000 + $25,000 = $200,000. The operating reserve covers five months at the illustrative $5,000 monthly run rate, not the entire 3–12 month first-deal window under every timing outcome.; stages: label: Parcel purchase capital; value: $140,000; 70.0%; numeric value: 140000.0; detail: Reserve cash for purchase prices and deposits credited against those prices. At the Base-Case $30,000 average purchase price, four simultaneous parcels use $120,000; do not count pending sales as available acquisition cash.; label: Diligence and preparation; value: $20,000; 10.0%; numeric value: 20000.0; detail: Fund surveys, environmental work, land-use verification, and narrowly scoped preparation. Track failed-deal investigation costs separately from successful parcel basis, and stop spending when a fatal defect emerges.; label: Closing and carrying liquidity; value: $15,000; 7.5%; numeric value: 15000.0; detail: Hold liquidity for settlement charges, property taxes, insurance, and parcel-specific carrying bills before sales replenish cash. Do not also allocate this same cash to recurring contractor or software invoices.; label: Operating runway; value: $25,000; 12.5%; numeric value: 25000.0; detail: Fund five months of recurring operations at $5,000 monthly. The canonical monthly range is $3,000–$15,000; a slower exit or higher burn requires fewer concurrent purchases, more capital, or lower spending.

text.title: Allocate $200,000 Before Making the First Offer
text.tspan: Allocate $200,000 Before Making the First Offer

rect.title: label: Parcel purchase capital; numeric value: 140000.0; value: $140,000; 70.0%; detail: Reserve cash for purchase prices and deposits credited against those prices. At the Base-Case $30,000 average purchase price, four simultaneous parcels use $120,000; do not count pending sales as available acquisition cash.

label: Diligence and preparation; numeric value: 20000.0; value: $20,000; 10.0%; detail: Fund surveys, environmental work, land-use verification, and narrowly scoped preparation. Track failed-deal investigation costs separately from successful parcel basis, and stop spending when a fatal defect emerges.

label: Closing and carrying liquidity; numeric value: 15000.0; value: $15,000; 7.5%; detail: Hold liquidity for settlement charges, property taxes, insurance, and parcel-specific carrying bills before sales replenish cash. Do not also allocate this same cash to recurring contractor or software invoices.

label: Operating runway; numeric value: 25000.0; value: $25,000; 12.5%; detail: Fund five months of recurring operations at $5,000 monthly. The canonical monthly range is $3,000–$15,000; a slower exit or higher burn requires fewer concurrent purchases, more capital, or lower spending.

text.title: Assumptions: This single startup allocation totals $200,000 and sits inside the canonical $50,000–$400,000 capital range. Values are USD capital allocations, not annual expenses or recognized revenue. Acquisition capital remains inventory until disposition; unused reserves remain cash. Recycling sale proceeds is required to support annual purchases above the initial inventory bucket.
